This week on Mixture of Experts, our team of panelists talk about big infrastructure changes and small models. IBM is teaming up with Together AI on a multi-year deal to build a massive inference cluster on IBM Cloud, powered by NVIDIA's newest chips. The goal: cheaper, faster access to open-source AI models for enterprises, with the cluster expected to go live in early 2027.

Then there's Meta, which just open-sourced Muse Glimmer—a 30B-parameter model small enough to run locally on your laptop's GPU. Think coding, function calling, and agent tasks, all without needing the cloud. But as models get smaller, what does it mean for larger AI providers?
